Athena Tests the Battle.
Odysseus, I have not forgotten you.
Mentor, keep ruin off me.
Remember the friend who honored you all his life.
Or have you come late on purpose, now the work is nearly done?
Odysseus rebukes him but first tests his strength by remaining disguised and partially withholding help.

Then the four cast as one, and four men fell, and the hall filled with the noise of the dying.
Athena raises her aegis from the roof beam and terror breaks the remaining formation.

The Hall Is Cleared.

Spare me, Odysseus, and pity me.
No man taught me my songs but a god, and I came into this hall under force, not for love of them.
Mark the order.
Them into the courtyard.
The living search the blood-filled hall for any remaining threat.

scenes.world: a dim stone banquet hall with timber roof beams, lit only by hearth fire and oil lamps, silent-era costume drama look; aftermath movement at jerky silent speed, bodies and smoke.

captain.asks: Pose-to-pose at silent speed: the pursuit through the hall, Leiodes's plea and death without cutting away, then the hall emptied.
diagnosis: Stone reliefs and statues carry the killing better than any live body; the cut becomes a museum.
Baroque facades and rock slopes break the hall; the courtyard exit is the one clean geography.
The pardon has no hand: the plea plays over carved clutter.

scenes.title: The Disloyal Maids
scenes.card: The nurse names twelve maids who sided with the suitors; they clean the hall and are hanged, and the goatherd killed.

subs.text: Scene seven.
The Disloyal Maids.
Identifies twelve maids who consorted with the suitors and mocked the household.
The women carried the bodies out under the porch,
and scoured the tables and the floor with water and sponges until the hall was clean.
No clean death for them, not by my sword.
They poured shame on my head and on my mother's while she lay alone.
They brought Melanthius down into the court and cut him apart, and gave what was left to the dogs.
So the house was emptied of its false servants,
and everything that had rotted inside it was carried out into the light.

scenes.world: a dim stone banquet hall with timber roof beams, lit only by hearth fire and oil lamps, silent-era costume drama look and its courtyard in grey daylight; harsh, unadorned, the violence kept to silhouette.

captain.asks: Pose-to-pose in harsh grey daylight: maids named, bodies carried, the hall scrubbed, the line of hanged figures in silhouette.
diagnosis: 1930s dresses, office tables and a plastic bin make the maids a secretarial pool.
The hanging is honest only once: shadows of figures on the ground; the cable is a coil and a tyre.
The Telemachus face is borrowed from the storeroom scene; continuity of the son holds by accident.

scenes.title: The House Calls Penelope
scenes.card: Odysseus purifies the hall with fire; loyal servants embrace him, and the nurse goes to wake the queen.

subs.text: Scene eight.
The House Calls Penelope.
Bring sulfur and fire so the hall can be purified.
Loyal women enter, recognize him, and embrace him in tears.
Odysseus receives them while restraining grief and maintaining security.
Odysseus sends Eurycleia upstairs to wake Penelope and announce that her husband has returned.

sign.name: Bodies of gest
sign.operation: Frontal wide of Odysseus carrying the sulphur fire through the hall, the women entering in a line, each embracing him.

scenes.world: a dim stone banquet hall with timber roof beams, lit only by hearth fire and oil lamps, silent-era costume drama look; morning after, thick sulphur smoke, flat white light through the haze.

captain.asks: Frontal wide: Odysseus carries the sulphur fire through the hall; the women enter in a line, each embracing him; the old nurse goes up the stair.
diagnosis: Hand-tinted colour stairs and a fairy-tale bedroom flood every row; refusing them is the whole job.
Smoke carries: the brazier interior and the cauldron are the cut's strongest bodies.
The embraces never happen; the line of women is seen from behind in modern coats.

prologue: The doors are locked, the weapons are gone, and the beggar holds the bow. Now Odysseus reveals himself and takes back his house by force.
